resources.string: Only the current record window is counted: the module keeps the latest %1$d groups (notifications with identical text and verdict merge into one), so clearing records resets these numbers. The module side holds the authoritative copy.

Nothing has been blocked in this window. Nothing is ever blocked while observe mode is on — turn it off in Settings to let verdicts take effect; otherwise check the framework log to confirm the verdict chain is running.
Observe mode is on: verdicts still run and are recorded, but nothing is blocked yet — the blocked count above stays 0 until you turn it off.
Planned: labelled set and fit status (threshold, delta version, delivery result), plus false-positive review.
Framework service: not connected (enable this module in LSPosed, then reopen this page; changes cannot be delivered while disconnected, so the controls are greyed out)
Connected to the framework service, but the live config cannot be read (corrupted?). The values below are defaults; changes can still be delivered.
%1$d labels will be deleted and cannot be restored. The model then falls back to the built-in one, and scores change back immediately.
Groups: %1$d · events: %2$d (cap: %3$d groups); showing the latest %4$d. The module side holds the authoritative copy.
Labels: %1$d · the authoritative copy is labels.json on the module side (it survives an app reinstall, just like records)

Marking a notification as spam or ham hands its text to on-device fine-tuning; once the sample threshold is reached the delta is fitted and pushed to the module side automatically (it applies to the next verdict) — no manual trigger.
(No records yet. Whether the verdict chain is running is visible in the framework log; module-side records live in /data/misc/notifyguard/logs.json)
Fetch timed out: the module is inactive, or the system framework has not been restarted since install (no data is lost — it is still under /data/misc/notifyguard on the module side)
The previous label action is still waiting for a reply
%1$s had no effect: the module side sent no reply (module inactive / system framework not restarted since install / labels.json corrupted)
This reads the module\'s live state, not a UI guess: safe mode, assembly failures and a disabled verdict path all show up here.
Module not responding (not enabled in LSPosed, system framework not restarted since install, or the status channel failed to register)
Safe mode: the verdict path is disabled, every notification passes
Hooks not installed: see the assembly details below
Slot hits %1$d · funnel verdicts %2$d · funnel pass-through %3$d · blocked by ROM %4$d · errors %5$d
AI model unavailable (that whole step passes)
Assembly this launch: OK %1$d / SKIP %2$d / FAIL %3$d (module version %4$s)
The flag watcher is running, so clearing the flag restores verdicts.
The flag watcher is unavailable, so restarting the system framework is still needed after clearing.
Switches are delivered the moment they are flicked, the threshold on release — there is no Save button on this screen.
when off, the chain passes everything (records are still written)
record only, never block: verdicts still run and reason still shows the AI score and the matched rule
on-device hashed n-gram + logistic regression, no network
A score ≥ the threshold blocks. The slider is greyed out while the switch above is off — the value takes no part in verdicts then. Lower is more aggressive; 0 blocks everything.
AI score threshold: no live value read (framework service not connected)
AI is off, so it has no effect
release to deliver, currently in effect %1$s
A match passes straight through, never reaching rules or AI: blocking one of these costs far more than missing an ad.
The config the module side actually reads right now (read-only). The switches above are rendered from it — check here first when \"I changed it but nothing happened\".
(not connected, no live config to read)
Framework service is not connected, the change was not delivered
Delivery failed, the switch was reverted to the live value
Delivery failed, the threshold was reverted to the live value
The clear request got no reply (the module side did not answer)
The safe-mode flag is still set: clearing failed, still in safe mode
Safe-mode flag cleared, verdicts are back
Safe-mode flag cleared, hooks are being reinstalled
Safe-mode flag cleared, but the flag watcher is unavailable: a system framework restart is still needed to restore verdicts
A match blocks. Matching is a lowercased substring test (not a regex), so AD and ad are the same rule.
when off the keywords stay in the config, they just take no part in verdicts
no keywords yet: this switch has nothing to enable until you fill them in and save
Delivering while you type would block notifications on a half-typed keyword, so only the button below submits; saving delivers immediately and takes effect on the module side.
Listed apps skip AI recognition; keyword rules still apply (those are explicit block requests).
Candidates come from package names seen in module-side records — those are the apps that actually posted a notification, so no \"read installed apps\" permission is needed.
No candidates yet: the module side has not recorded any notification, or neither this page nor the records page has pulled yet. You can type a package name below.
Only the first %1$d are listed (whitelisted ones first). If the app you want to allow is not among them, type its package name below.
Save failed: the framework service is not connected
Save failed: delivery did not go through (the module side still has the previous config)
Keywords cleared and delivered: the rule no longer blocks anything
Saved %1$d keywords and delivered them (effective on the module side right away)
No keywords yet: fill them in below and save first
Keyword rule disabled (the keywords stay in the config)
%1$s added to the whitelist: its notifications skip AI recognition (keyword rules still apply)
Delivery failed, the whitelist was reverted to the live value
Bad package name: expected something like com.example.app (a package name, not an app label)
Candidate fetch timed out: the module is inactive, or the system framework has not been restarted since install (existing candidates still work)
Fine-tuning: not delivered (auto-fits once there are %1$d labels with at least %2$d per class)
Fine-tuning: not delivered (trainable samples %1$d/%2$d, spam %3$d/%4$d, ham %5$d/%6$d)
Fine-tuning: delivered v%1$s (the version number is written but the delta file cannot be read — the module side scores with the plain base model)
